page.layout: One page of running text, with a marginal note in the right margin beside the decree. Running head and page number at the top, catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: tes jam tum respectantis impedita omnia, atque ita sensim directa res, ut oppressis melioribus in civitate, & in carcerem detrusis, conspirantibus cum eo, quibus odium religionis, studium rerum suarum, patriae incuria inerat, civitas in partes Hispanicas sit delapsa. In eo rerum suarum statu civitas actionibus partis adversae provocata controversiam, & conditionem suam ad Principem Parmensem; qui tum pro rege Belgio praesidebat, retulit, ejusque opem rogavit. Parmensis ex libellis & adjunctis documentis causâ cognitâ, & cum secreto Senatu regio communicatâ, ex ejus sententiâ inDecretum Principis Parme-fis, Belgii gubernato-ris. hunc modum decrevit: Ob studium tuendae servandaeque Romanae Catholicae religionis, & fidem ac obsequium constans erga regem Groningani habento ad tempus totum jus Stapulae rerum promercalium tàm peregrinarum quàm in agro vicino nascentium. Oldermanno potestas esto contra hoc jus delinquentes ad tribunal societatis mercatorum huic quaestioni destinatu m trahere, ac reos agere; condemnatique si velint Senatum

page.notes: Right margin note: "Decretum Principis Parmensis, Belgii gubernatoris." Transcribed with printed line-end hyphens. The reading "Parme-fis" at the line end is doubtful: the scan shows a mark over the e, so it may be "Parmen-sis" [?]. The word "destinatu m" has a space that is probably a printing error, left as printed. The decree text from "Ob studium" to "Senatum" is in italics. "Senatum" is the catchword, set in italics at the foot. The signature "N 2" has a small 2. The faint watermark at the bottom right is a digitiser's mark and is not transcribed.
